problem: E26 built a common Currency Contract reporting shape but had not yet been used to actually DRIVE a real development decision -- only to describe 2 real subjects side by side.

decision.decision_summary: Re-applied the Contract to both real subjects (Index=STALE, Pointer=CURRENT, both identical to their raw Guard results). Applied the Currency-aware rule (STALE=not authoritative, CURRENT=reusable) as the actual real decision input, then used it to re-validate E26's own cached refresh candidate: CANDIDATE_STALE_BUT_EXPECTED_DYNAMIC_NOT_CHASED. Index NOT refreshed (unbounded self-improvement explicitly avoided).

action.action_summary: Re-ran both real Guards unmodified; confirmed Contract<->raw-Guard full agreement; compared E26's cached candidate against fresh real data (candidate_still_valid=false); made 0 modifications to the Index or pointer chain.

result.note: Uses the Contract as a real decision input; does not refresh the Index, does not modify the pointer chain, does not change this Goal's own real status.

cause.root_cause_summary: A reporting contract (E26) is only useful once something real actually consumes it to make a decision -- that consumption step had not yet happened.

lesson: Using a Currency Contract as a real decision input surfaced a genuine, self-referential edge case (a cached refresh candidate going stale the moment new real data arrives) -- and the correct, mature response was to recognize it as the SAME already-understood dynamic and deliberately decline to chase it further, rather than spawning an endless chain of ever-staler refresh candidates.
